transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, my mind just keeps going blank at the worst possible times. I'm a crossing guard, and lately, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly can't remember what to do. It's like the steps I've done for years just vanish from my head.
When your mind goes blank like that, are you aware it's happening in the moment, or do you only realize afterward that you've lost time or forgotten what you were doing?

I am aware it's happening right in the moment. It's not like I lose time or black out or anything. I'll just be standing there... like I was saying with the closure forms or holding my paddle. I know I'm at work, and I know I need to do something, but my brain just completely empties out. 

I'm looking right at the equipment, fully realizing that I can't remember the steps to do my job, and I just can't make myself think of what comes next. The thoughts just aren't there.
When your mind goes blank like that, do you notice your heart racing, feel sweaty, or experience a sense of panic or intense worry right before or during these episodes?

No, not really. I don't feel panicked or sweaty, and my heart isn't racing. It's just... quiet. Like the thoughts are just gone. I don't feel anxious about it until maybe later when I realize how dangerous it could be, but in the moment, it's just a blank.
How often are these blank episodes happening? Are we talking about several times a day, a few times a week, or less frequently than that?

It's happening pretty much every day now. I'd say several times a day. Like I was saying earlier about looking at the forms or holding the paddle... the steps I've done for years just keep vanishing on me over and over. So, yeah, it's definitely multiple times a shift at this point.

Before these blank episodes started happening, did you experience any head injuries, high fevers or infections, or any significant changes in your health? Also, are you taking any new medications or using any substances?

No, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or been sick with a fever or anything. My health has been pretty much the same as always, aside from all this happening. And no, I haven't started any new medications, and I don't use any drugs or anything like that.

During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you feel disconnected from your body or surroundings, like you're watching yourself from outside, or does everything around you feel unreal or distant?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel like I'm outside my body or anything like that. And things don't really feel unreal... it's just that the thoughts I need are missing. I'm still right there, holding the sign or looking at the paper, I just... I just don't know what to do next. It's not a disconnected feeling, just an empty one.

Besides these blank moments with your job tasks, have you noticed any other changes in your memory—like forgetting conversations you had, misplacing things, or having trouble remembering people's names or recent events in your personal life?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed anything like that. I remember conversations fine, and I know where I put my keys and everything. It's really just the... the steps for my job that keep disappearing. My memory for everything else seems to be working exactly the same as it always has.
When did these blank episodes first start happening? Did they begin suddenly, or have you noticed them gradually getting worse over weeks or months?

It's been going on for about a year and eight months now. They started happening right after my closest friend died. So I guess it wasn't really a gradual thing over months... it just kind of began after that happened.

When you're doing other routine activities that you've practiced many times—like driving, cooking a meal, or getting dressed—do you ever experience the same kind of blank moments where you forget the steps, or is it really only happening with your crossing guard duties?

No, things like driving and cooking are fine. It really just happens at work. That's exactly why I came in, actually, because my mind just keeps going blank at the absolute worst times. I will look at the road-closure forms, or I'll be holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps I have done for years.
